newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-NO CHANGE IN SPAIN AS TOP FOUR DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO CHANGE IN SPAIN AS TOP FOUR DRAW.

text.p: Real Madrid missed the chance to open an 11-point lead in the Spanish championship on Sunday when they drew 1-1 at Tenerife -- hours after their nearest challengers were also held to draws.
Madrid now lead the standings by nine points from Barcelona, who drew 1-1 at Valencia, and Real Betis, who fought out a goalless draw at Espanyol.
Deportivo La Coruna are a further three points adrift in fourth place following their 1-1 draw at Real Sociedad on Saturday.
Real Madrid went ahead in the 59th minute through Victor Sanchez, only to see Oliver Neuville knock in the equaliser seven minutes later.

Even so the league leaders will be happy to have survived a game that traditionally gives them problems. Real had seen their attempts to have the game postponed because of injuries and international duty rejected by the Spanish Federation.

Barcelona fought back bravely after going behind to a goal just before halftime by Valencia's Leandro, but in the end had a mistake by their former goalkeeper, Andoni Zubizarreta, to thank for their draw.
Zubizarreta was badly positioned for a Hristo Stoichkov cross which found Ronaldo completely unmarked at the far post midway through the second half.
But draws are not enough for Barca who now have just 11 games left to close the gap.

Real Betis failed to score for only the second time this season. A missed chance in the last minute of the game proved costly -- a goal would have ensured second place and with it a provisional place in the European Cup for next season.
Betis still trail Barcelona on goal difference.
Hercules picked up their seventh win of the season, 2-1 at Racing Santander, but stay bottom on goal difference after Sevilla drew 2-2 at home with Valladolid.
Champions Atletico Madrid are out of contention for the title and will stay fifth regardless of the result of Monday's game with Sporting Gijon.
